title: Taking Your Club on a Rwanda Golf Trip? Play Kigali's 18 Holes, Then Meet the Gorillas
meta_title: Rwanda Golf Trip for Clubs: Kigali Golf and Gorillas
meta_description: Plan a Rwanda golf trip for your club: Kigali Golf Resort, Falcon on Lake Muhazi, gorilla permits for groups, a 6-day plan and costs per person.
excerpt: A Rwanda golf trip pairs Kigali Golf Resort's 18 holes with a gorilla trek in Volcanoes National Park in five or six days. Here is how clubs handle permits, golf bags, rooming and costs.
content:
A Rwanda golf trip pairs a round or two at Kigali Golf Resort, the country's 18-hole Gary Player Design course, with a morning beside mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park, about 2.5 hours north by road. Five or six days is enough, and the distances are short enough that a club never wastes a day in transit.

The hard part for a club captain or society secretary is the planning: gorilla permits are capped at eight people per family, golf bags compete with trekking luggage for space, and not every partner wants to play. This guide covers the courses, a day-by-day plan, permits, vehicles, rooming and costs by tier, and shows how our club and society safaris team in Nairobi puts a Rwanda golf trip together for a private group.

Quick Facts

  • Main course: Kigali Golf Resort and Villas, 18 holes on about 52 hectares in the city (Visit Rwanda)
  • Second course: Falcon Golf and Country Club, 9 holes on Lake Muhazi, Rwamagana District, about an hour east of Kigali
  • Gorilla permit: USD 1,500 per foreign non-resident adult (Rwanda Development Board, checked November 2026)
  • Group cap: 8 trekkers per gorilla family per day; 10 habituated families open to visitors
  • Minimum trekking age: 15 years
  • Kigali to Musanze: about 2.5 hours by road
  • Best months for a Rwanda golf trip: June to September and December to February, the two drier spells

What Does a Rwanda Golf Trip Actually Involve?

A Rwanda golf trip involves golf in and around Kigali at the start or end, and a gorilla trek in the Virunga volcanoes in the middle. Kigali has the courses, the hotels and the international airport; Volcanoes National Park has the gorillas. Everything else on the trip is about linking the two comfortably.

That simple shape is why Rwanda suits a golf society better than most safari countries. There are no internal flights, no long dirt roads and no need to choose between a golf holiday and a wildlife trip. Your group plays, travels north on good tarmac, treks, and is back in Kigali for a final round or the flight home.

Kigali Golf Resort and Villas

Kigali Golf Resort is the course your Rwanda golf trip is built around. Gary Player Design rebuilt the old nine-hole Kigali Golf Club into a full 18 holes, and the course was unveiled in August 2021. It sits in the Nyarutarama and Kacyiru area of the city, with nine lakes, 23 bridges and three rain shelters across the layout, according to reporting at the launch.

The course is owned through an investment arm of the Rwanda Social Security Board and has a clubhouse and a golf academy. For a visiting group, its best feature is location: you can play a morning round and be at a city hotel for lunch. Visit Rwanda's golf page describes it as the country's premier 18-hole course.

Falcon Golf and Country Club on Lake Muhazi

Falcon Golf and Country Club is a nine-hole course on the banks of Lake Muhazi in Rwamagana District, Eastern Province, about an hour from Kigali. It opened in 2013 with a pro-am, and the lakeside setting makes it a pleasant change of scene for a second day of golf on a Rwanda golf trip, or a relaxed outing for players who prefer nine holes.

CourseHoles and settingHow a club might use it
Kigali Golf Resort and Villas18 holes, Gary Player Design, in KigaliMain competition round, ideally on arrival day plus one or the final morning
Falcon Golf and Country Club9 holes on Lake Muhazi, about 1 hour east of KigaliRelaxed second outing, or a half-day for higher handicaps and partners
Volcanoes National ParkNo golf; gorilla and golden monkey treks from KinigiThe centrepiece day, with a second activity for non-trekkers

How Many Days Should a Club Plan?

A club should plan five days as the minimum and six as the comfortable length for a Rwanda golf trip with gorillas. Five days gives one round and one trek; six adds a second round or a buffer day; seven or eight lets you finish beside Lake Kivu or add a game drive in Akagera National Park.

Our 5-day luxury Rwanda golf and mountain gorilla trekking tour is the template we adapt for clubs: arrival in Kigali, a round at Kigali Golf Resort with rental clubs and a cart, the Kigali Genocide Memorial and the drive to Musanze, the gorilla trek, then the return. For a larger society we usually stretch it to six days, like the sample below.

DayPlanOvernight
Day 1Arrive at Kigali International Airport, meet the guides, settle in and hold a welcome dinnerKigali
Day 2Morning round at Kigali Golf Resort; afternoon free or a short city tourKigali
Day 3Kigali Genocide Memorial, then about 2.5 hours north to Musanze; gorilla briefing over dinnerMusanze or Kinigi
Day 4Gorilla trek from the 07:00 Kinigi briefing; golden monkeys or a village visit for non-trekkersMusanze or Kinigi
Day 5Drive back to Kigali; afternoon nine holes at Falcon on Lake Muhazi or a second Kigali roundKigali
Day 6Final breakfast, prize-giving and airport transferDeparture

If the club wants a slower finish to its Rwanda golf trip, swap day 5 for two nights on Lake Kivu at Rubavu or Karongi before returning to Kigali. Groups that want savannah wildlife as well can look at our 6-day Rwanda celebration safari, which adds Akagera to gorillas and golden monkeys and can take a golf day at either end.

Gorilla Day: Permits, Group Sizes and Fitness

Gorilla day on a Rwanda golf trip runs on the park's rules. Permits cost USD 1,500 per foreign non-resident adult, eight visitors can join each family per day, trekkers must be 15 or older, and the Kinigi briefing starts at 07:00, according to the Rwanda Development Board's gorilla tracking page (checked November 2026).

Volcanoes National Park has ten habituated families open to visitors, so a club of 16 is split across two families and a club of 24 across three, all on the same morning. Your guides then regroup everyone at the park headquarters for the drive back. Our Rwanda gorilla permit guide explains the booking process, the cancellation terms and the promotional rates the Rwanda Development Board offers outside June to October.

Once with the gorillas, you have one hour, must stay seven metres away and may not use flash. Anyone with a cold or flu should not trek, because gorillas catch human illnesses; a golfer who wakes up sniffling will be asked to stay behind, so do not plan the trek for the day after a long-haul flight.

How fit do golfers need to be?

Golfers on a Rwanda golf trip who walk 18 holes comfortably are usually fit enough to trek, but the terrain is steeper and muddier than any fairway. Treks can last from one to six hours depending on where the family has moved. Rangers try to match slower walkers to closer families, and porters can carry day packs. Our guide to how hard gorilla trekking really is covers altitude and pacing in more detail.

Partners who would rather not trek

Partners on a Rwanda golf trip who would rather not trek still have a good day in the Virungas. Golden monkey trekking is shorter and gentler, with permits of USD 100 for foreign visitors (checked November 2026), and the Musanze area also offers cultural visits and the Ellen DeGeneres Campus of the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund. Booking this second programme at the same time as the gorilla permits keeps the day fair for everyone.

Vehicles, Rooming and Golf Bags: What the Organiser Should Sort Early

The organiser of a Rwanda golf trip should settle three things before anything else: how many vehicles the group needs once golf bags are counted, who shares rooms with whom, and the final names for the gorilla permits. Those three decisions drive most of the cost and most of the stress.

Vehicles and luggage

On a Rwanda golf trip, safari 4x4s seat six or seven, but a full golf bag takes the space of a person. When players bring their own clubs, plan on four or five golfers per vehicle or add a luggage van that follows the group. Renting clubs at Kigali Golf Resort removes the problem entirely, which is why many clubs leave their bags at home and bring only shoes and gloves.

Rooming and single travellers

Most club groups on a Rwanda golf trip mix couples, friends sharing twin rooms and a few single travellers. Lodges near Volcanoes are smaller than Kigali hotels, so ask for the rooming list early and agree in advance who pays any single supplement. One shared booking for the whole group also means one deposit schedule, one set of terms and one person to call.

Why a private club trip beats joining a scheduled tour

A private Rwanda golf trip for your club means your own tee times, your own vehicles and a gorilla day built around your group's fitness, not a stranger's. You set the pace, run your own competition and keep the evenings for the club. Our step-by-step guide to organising a group safari shows how we collect names, deposits and passport details so the captain is not chasing everyone alone.

What Does a Rwanda Golf Trip Cost Per Person?

A six-day Rwanda golf trip with one gorilla trek costs roughly USD 3,500 to 4,500 per person at mid-range level and USD 7,000 or more at the luxury end, sharing rooms and excluding international flights. These are estimates; the gorilla permit alone is USD 1,500 of each trekker's total.

Travel styleEstimated cost per person (6 days)What changes
ComfortUSD 3,000 to 3,500Good-value city hotel and simple lodges near Musanze, rental clubs, shared vehicles
Mid-rangeUSD 3,500 to 4,500Upmarket Kigali hotel, comfortable lodge near Kinigi, two rounds of golf
LuxuryUSD 7,000 and upTop Kigali hotel and a premium lodge beside the park, private guiding throughout

Group pricing on a Rwanda golf trip works in the club's favour on shared costs. Vehicles, guides and fuel are divided across more people as the group grows, while permits, park activities, green fees and rooms stay fixed per person. That is why a society of 12 usually pays less per head than a party of four on the same itinerary. Golf fees, club hire and carts are quoted directly by the course, and we build them into the final quote.

When Is the Best Time for Golf and Gorillas?

The best time for a Rwanda golf trip is June to September or December to February, the two drier spells, when fairways are firmer and forest trails are less slippery. Both golf and gorilla trekking run all year, though, and the wetter months bring quieter lodges and the Rwanda Development Board's promotional permit rates.

The long rains, roughly March to May, are the hardest months for a Rwanda golf trip, because a washed-out round is harder to reschedule than a muddy trek. The short rains around October to mid-December are more manageable, with showers that usually pass. Whatever the month, book gorilla permits as soon as you have names; for July, August and the Christmas weeks that can mean a year ahead.

Visas and entry

Before a Rwanda golf trip, check the entry rules. Visitors from Commonwealth countries, including the UK, can get a free 30-day visa on arrival in Rwanda, with a passport valid for at least six months, according to UK government travel advice (checked November 2026). Other nationalities should check Rwanda's current immigration rules before booking. A yellow fever certificate is needed if you arrive from a country with a risk of transmission.

Clubs that want a longer golf safari can compare Rwanda with East Africa's other options: our post on the Serengeti golf course at Fort Ikoma covers savannah golf in Tanzania, and our Kigali conference and gorilla trekking guide helps if some members are combining the trip with work.

Insider Tips

  • Book permits first: gorilla permits, then the Musanze lodge, then tee times; golf is the easiest piece to move
  • Play golf before the trek: tired legs after a six-hour trek make for a poor round the next morning
  • Collect passport details early: every gorilla permit is issued in the trekker's name
  • Pack for both: golf shoes and gloves, plus waterproof boots, gardening gloves for nettles and a rain jacket; see our gorilla trekking packing list
  • Leave a buffer: one spare half-day on any Rwanda golf trip lets you move a rained-off round without touching the trek
  • Name one club contact: a single organiser who confirms names, rooming and payments saves days of back-and-forth

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days does a Rwanda golf trip with gorillas need?

A Rwanda golf trip with a gorilla trek needs five or six days for most clubs. That allows one or two rounds at Kigali Golf Resort, a day to reach Musanze, the trek and a spare morning. Seven or eight days lets the group add Lake Kivu or a game drive in Akagera.

How many golf courses are there in Rwanda?

Rwanda has two courses that a visiting club would plan around. Kigali Golf Resort and Villas is the country's 18-hole championship course, set on about 52 hectares in the city, and Falcon Golf and Country Club is a nine-hole course on the shore of Lake Muhazi in Rwamagana District, roughly an hour east of Kigali.

Can a whole golf club trek gorillas on the same day in Rwanda?

A whole golf club on a Rwanda golf trip can trek on the same day if permits are booked early. Each habituated gorilla family takes a maximum of eight visitors a day, so a group of 16 is split across two families and a group of 24 across three. Everyone attends the same 07:00 briefing at Kinigi and returns by early afternoon.

How much is a gorilla permit for a golf group in Rwanda?

A gorilla permit in Rwanda costs USD 1,500 per foreign non-resident adult, according to the Rwanda Development Board (checked November 2026). There is no group rate, and the permit is the same whether you trek in a party of two or join a club of twenty. The Rwanda Development Board offers promotional rates outside June to October, so confirm current terms before booking.

Do golfers need to bring their own clubs to Rwanda?

Golfers do not need to bring clubs to Rwanda, because Kigali Golf Resort offers rental sets and carts, and our golf and gorilla itinerary includes them. Many club players still bring their own bag for a better fit. If they do, tell us early so the vehicles have room for bags as well as trekking luggage.

Final Thoughts

A Rwanda golf trip works because Kigali's 18 holes and the gorillas of Volcanoes National Park sit a short, easy drive apart, so a club can play, trek and celebrate inside a week. Secure the permits first, decide early about golf bags and rooming, and keep a spare half-day for the weather.
